walkthroughs.body_html:
Steps must be clear, ordered and replicable.

State variables, apparatus, key volumes, and how data is recorded.

Systematic: e.g. wrong scale zero -> shift all data.

Random: e.g. judging end-point -> scatters.

mcqs.q: Random errors can be reduced by:
What kind of bond forms between a ligand and a central metal ion in a complex?
options: Transition metals are coloured because their nuclei emit photons in the visible range.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
A dative (coordinate) covalent bond — the ligand donates a lone pair into an empty orbital on the metal.
The ligand forms an ionic bond with the metal because the metal is positively charged.

mcqs.q: Why are most transition metal complex ions coloured?
options: Transition metal ions are coloured because they have a half-full d-subshell which naturally absorbs light.
Transition metals are coloured because their nuclei emit photons in the visible range.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they can gain protons easily.
Ligands split the d-orbitals into two energy levels; electrons absorb visible light to jump between them (d-d transitions), and the complementary colour is transmitted.

mcqs.q: Why can transition metals show variable oxidation states?
options: Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they can gain protons easily.
Transition metals have variable oxidation states because they have many shells of electrons.
Transition metals are coloured because their nuclei emit photons in the visible range.
The 4s and 3d orbitals are similar in energy, so different numbers of electrons can be removed without a large energy cost.
